Independent spectral reconstruction and the Brouwer e=2 Grassmann spectrum
correctness.rationale: Counting projective points gives BBᵀ=([n−1]_q−1)I+J and BᵀB=(q+1)I+A, so the adjacency sectors have dimensions 1, m−1 and N−m, with last two eigenvalues θ₁=[n−1]_q−q−2>0 and θ₂=−(q+1). Here N>m for n≥4. For b=2^p the distance-power matrix is bJ−bI+(1−b)A; its contrast eigenvalues are −b+(1−b)θ₁<0 and qb−(q+1). This proves the exact CND and strictness thresholds; centering kills just the constants in the strict case and additionally the θ₂ sector at equality. Counts of differing point indicators give squared distances 1 and (q+1)/q after scaling by 1/√(2q). In K=(1−t^b)I+(t−t^b)A+t^bJ, t=e^(−a), the constant and θ₁ sectors are positive for 0<t<1; the remaining eigenvalue is 1−(q+1)t+qt^b. This function decreases to zero at t=1 when b≤1+1/q. Otherwise it is strictly convex, positive at zero, zero with positive slope at one, and has exactly one interior root. At that root only the last sector drops out, leaving rank m; a=0 separately gives J of rank one. At p=1 factorization as (1−t)(1−qt) gives a≥log q on the nonzero branch.

evidence: Sánchez gives a finite-metric negative-type determinant criterion; Murugan gives its vertex-transitive graph counterpart and equality-kernel characterization. Resultary record 9535d19cf47d concerns different, diameter-four generalized-quadrangle graphs. Harandi et al. use real continuous Grassmannian geometry, not a finite-field path metric.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The generic negative-type criteria apply, but the distance-two spectral identity suffices directly. The other kernel records concern different schemes or geometry and are not needed to derive this conclusion.

evidence: On any diameter-two graph a radial matrix with values c₀,c₁,c₂ is (c₀−c₂)I+(c₁−c₂)A+c₂J. Use (0,1,2^p) or (1,t,t^(2^p)). The complete resulting sign and rank calculation is in the correctness assessment.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Substitute the prior table into that identity, test the two contrast scalars, and check the derivative at one and convexity. The minimal Euclidean dimension is the centered Gram rank. Even the displayed embedding is the standard point-incidence indicator with common normalization; its distances simply count the symmetric differences. Thus the exact formulas are routine consequences even without a prior verbatim classification.

evidence: The distinct two-column rank-metric record c3f4dc85f1e2 has the same threshold, scalar root and log q cutoff, but different space, multiplicities and Euclidean dimensions. The three-subspace Grassmann record 6313d9deadb2 has a different graph and threshold equation.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Two-column maps into a fixed complement embed by their graphs as an isometric subset of the Grassmannian when the target has dimension n−2, since intersection of the graphs is the kernel of the map difference. Thus the scalar cutoffs overlap, but restricting to this subset cannot establish sufficiency or global ranks on the whole Grassmannian. Neither matched theorem alone is equivalent.

value.rationale: Admissible radial kernels and minimal embedding dimensions are meaningful invariants. Here, however, all the claimed exact quantities are immediate sign or multiplicity readouts from the existing spectrum. The self-contained incidence proof is useful exposition, but the record gives no nonmechanical exact fact beyond those readouts.
